h1: The 6 Best E-Readers With Audiobook Support of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best E-Readers With Audiobooks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six e-readers that play audiobooks, sorted by store support, Bluetooth, text to speech, speaker and display type.
summary: The Kobo Libra Colour is the best e-reader for audiobooks, with a native store, Bluetooth pairing and a waterproof color screen. The PocketBook InkPad Color 3 adds a built-in speaker, and the Verse Pro Color is the compact color option. The OBOOK6 is the cheap route if you will install your own audiobook app.
intro: Bluetooth on an e-reader is not an audiobook feature. It only sends sound out, so the device still needs a way to get a narrated book in the first place. In this category there are exactly three routes: a native audiobook store, text to speech that reads any ebook in a synthetic voice, or an Android device where you install a third-party app.

Buyers who skip that distinction end up with a reader that cannot play the audiobooks they already own. Six devices were assessed from spec sheets and owner-reported audio use, then ranked on how directly each plays audiobooks, along with Bluetooth, speaker options, storage, display type and value. Android models with weak audio claims and a duplicate color variant were left out.

products.name: Kobo Libra Colour, 7" Glare-Free Colour E Ink Kaleido 3, Waterproof, Black
products.verdict: The only pick here with a native audiobook store built in.
products.description:
The Kobo Libra Colour pairs a 7 inch color E Ink Kaleido 3 screen with Kobo Audiobooks support, Bluetooth headphone pairing and a waterproof body. Having a store inside the device matters most: you buy, download and play a narrated book without sideloading files or hunting for an app that works on e-ink hardware.

Nothing else in this list ships with a native audiobook store, so the Kobo works the day you unbox it, which settles the ranking. The InkPad Color 3 below has a bigger screen and speaker, but relies on text to speech rather than a store.

Buy it if you want one library for ebooks and audio. The caveat is lock-in: you are tied to the Kobo ecosystem, and it sits in the top price bracket, so skip it if you already subscribe elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Readers wanting one library for ebooks and audio.
products.skipIf: You already subscribe to another audiobook service.

products.name: PocketBook InkPad Color 3, 7.8" Color E-Paper Display, Built-In Speaker
products.verdict: Plays audio out loud with no headphones, on a big 7.8 inch screen.
products.description:
The PocketBook InkPad Color 3 has a 7.8 inch color E Paper display, a built-in speaker, text to speech and Bluetooth. The speaker is unusual on an e-reader and lets you listen in a kitchen or workshop without pairing anything. It is the largest screen in the ranking, which helps with comics and cookbooks.

It ranks second because no native audiobook store is named. Audio comes from text to speech or files you load, so the experience is flatter than the Kobo's narrated store. It beats the Verse Pro Color on screen size and speaker.

Buy it for listening without headphones. The caveat is the sound: e-reader speakers are thin, and the top price bracket is steep if what you want is a narrated audiobook library.
products.idealFor: Listeners who do not want headphones.
products.skipIf: You want a native audiobook store.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro Color, 6" E Ink Kaleido 3, Text-to-Speech & Bluetooth
products.verdict: A pocketable color reader with text to speech and IPX8 waterproofing.
products.description:
The PocketBook Verse Pro Color is a 6 inch color Kaleido 3 reader with text to speech, Bluetooth and IPX8 waterproofing. A rating like IPX8 means submersion is within spec, which beats a vague waterproof claim. Its smaller body slips into a coat pocket.

It ranks third since it lists no built-in speaker, so audio goes through Bluetooth headphones, and the voice is synthetic. Against the Verse Pro below, you pay for the color screen, which suits covers and comics, though it is a little less sharp for text.

Buy it if you want a compact color reader that can read aloud. Skip it if you want narrated audiobooks, because text to speech cannot match professional narration, and the Kobo Libra Colour above is the better fit.
products.idealFor: Color readers wanting a compact body.

products.name: PocketBook Verse Pro E-Reader Waterproof, 6" E-Ink Carta HD, Azure
products.verdict: A waterproof black and white reader sold as an audiobook and ebook device.
products.description:
The PocketBook Verse Pro is a 6 inch E Ink Carta HD reader with 16GB of storage, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a waterproof body, sold as an audiobook and ebook device. Sixteen gigabytes is plenty, since audiobooks can run to hundreds of megabytes each, while ebooks barely register.

It ranks fourth because the screen is black and white and no built-in speaker is listed, so it needs headphones for sound. It costs less than the color Verse Pro, which is its advantage over the model above it.

Buy it as an affordable way to carry both text and audio on a small body. The caveat is the display: if you want color pages, step up to the Verse Pro Color or the Kobo. Without a native store, you load audio yourself.
products.idealFor: Affordable audio and text on a small body.

products.name: PocketBook Era Lite, Affordable 7" e-Reader, Bluetooth & Text-to-Speech Support
products.verdict: A large 7 inch reader with text to speech and up to two months of battery.
products.description:
The PocketBook Era Lite is a 7 inch reader with text to speech, Bluetooth and a listed battery life of up to two months. Long battery life matters on an e-reader that plays audio, because speech and Bluetooth draw more power than page turns alone.

It ranks fifth since it has no waterproofing listed and text to speech is its only audio route. The larger 7 inch screen is its edge over the 6 inch Verse Pro models, which are waterproof and smaller.

Buy it if you read far more than you listen and want a big screen with long battery life. Skip it if audiobooks are your main use, because a synthetic voice is a poor substitute for narration, and the Kobo or PocketBook InkPad Color 3 do the job better.

products.name: OBOOK6 eReader (32GB), 6" 300ppi Glare-Free Display, Android
products.verdict: A cheap Android reader that lets you install your own audiobook apps.
products.description:
The OBOOK6 is a 6 inch Android e-reader with 32GB of storage and a 300ppi glare-free display, running a genuine Android system. Android means you install the audiobook app you already use, whether a subscription service or a library app, which no locked-down reader here can do.

It ranks last because that freedom comes with effort. Audio depends on third-party apps, setup takes work, and it sits in the lowest price tier, where support and screen polish are weaker than the Kobo or PocketBook models.

Buy it if you already have an audiobook app and want a cheap screen to run it. Skip it if you want everything to work out of the box, because the Kobo Libra Colour does exactly that.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with an existing audiobook app.
products.skipIf: You want everything to work out of the box.

whatMatters.detail: There are three ways an e-reader plays audio. A native store, like Kobo's, sells and plays audiobooks directly. Text to speech reads any ebook aloud in a synthetic voice, and Android devices run third-party apps. Check which path your device uses before assuming your current subscription will work, because most dedicated readers cannot run apps from other stores.

Bluetooth sends audio to headphones or a speaker, and without it an e-reader can only play through a built-in speaker. Most devices here list it. Look for the word Bluetooth in the title or spec bullets rather than assuming it, and confirm whether the listing means audio output or only a connection to accessories.

A built-in speaker lets you listen without headphones, which suits kitchens, workshops and cars. Only the PocketBook InkPad Color 3 lists one in this guide. Treat it as a convenience, not a substitute for earbuds, since e-reader speakers are small and sound thin. Look for the word speaker in the listing title or specifications, not just audio support.

Audiobooks can run to hundreds of megabytes each, while ebooks are tiny. A device with 16GB or 32GB holds a real audio library, while a small drive fills quickly if you download several long titles. Find the storage figure in the listing, and check whether the device supports a memory card or only the built-in space.

Color E Ink suits book covers, comics and cookbooks, but is a little less sharp for plain text than black-and-white Carta HD. Waterproofing protects the device in a bath or by the pool. Check for an IPX rating, such as IPX8, or the word waterproof in the title, because many readers do not state either.

faq.q: Do all e-readers with Bluetooth play audiobooks?
faq.a: No. Bluetooth only sends audio out, so the device still needs a way to get audiobooks, whether a store like the Kobo Libra Colour has, text to speech or an Android app on the OBOOK6. Check the audiobook path first.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming an existing subscription will work. Most dedicated e-readers cannot run apps from other stores, so confirm compatibility before buying. Only the Android OBOOK6 lets you install your own audiobook app freely.

faq.q: Is text to speech as good as an audiobook?
faq.a: No. It is a synthetic voice reading the text, which is useful on the PocketBook Verse Pro Color or Era Lite but flatter than professional narration. For narrated books, the Kobo Libra Colour with its audiobook store is the better fit.

faq.q: How do I pair Bluetooth headphones?
faq.a: Open the Bluetooth setting on the device, put your headphones in pairing mode and select them from the list. The Kobo Libra Colour and PocketBook models list Bluetooth, and once paired, the device usually reconnects automatically.

faq.q: How much storage do I need for audiobooks?
faq.a: A single audiobook can take several hundred megabytes, so 16GB or more is comfortable for a library. The PocketBook Verse Pro lists 16GB and the OBOOK6 32GB. Check the figure in the listing, as it varies widely.

faq.q: Can I use these in the bath?
faq.a: The Kobo Libra Colour is waterproof and the PocketBook Verse Pro Color lists IPX8, and the Verse Pro also lists a waterproof body. Others do not state waterproofing, so keep them away from water.

finalTake: The Kobo Libra Colour is the right e-reader for anyone who wants narrated audiobooks without fuss, since the store, Bluetooth and waterproofing arrive together. Pick the PocketBook InkPad Color 3 if a speaker matters, or the OBOOK6 if you will install your own app. Settle the audiobook path before comparing screens.
